### Observed differences

- Activity A02 was completely absent in the earlier window (0 of 200 cases) and is executed in every case in the later window (200 of 200), exactly once per case with no repetitions [OCC001].
- In the later window A02 always occupies the same relative position (position 1.0 in every case, no spread), i.e. a fixed slot at the end of the case; in the earlier window it had no position because it never occurred [POS001].
- Before, A06 effectively terminated the case: it ran in all 200 cases at a mean relative position of about 0.99, and only 4 outgoing transitions from it were observed (all to A04). In the later window, all 200 observed outgoing transitions of A06 go to A02, and A06's mean relative position dropped to about 0.79 [DIR005, POS005].
- In the later window A01, A03 and A04 each precede A02 in 100 in 100 cases; A05, which is optional, co-occurs with A02 in about 53 in 100 cases (before it), while about 47 in 100 cases run A02 without any A05. In the earlier window these co-occurrences did not exist because A02 never ran [REL001, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006].
- The other activities all shifted to slightly earlier relative positions (A03 mean 0.48 → 0.36, A04 0.36 → 0.28, A05 0.69 → 0.58, A06 0.99 → 0.79), a pattern consistent with one fixed step being appended at the end rather than with several activities being moved individually [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A02 was added as a new, mandatory final step: in the later window every case executes A02 exactly once at a fixed end position, directly after A06, which in the earlier window was the last activity of the case. This is shown directly from three angles that agree: participation (0 of 200 cases before, 200 of 200 after, always exactly one occurrence), position (a constant final position for A02, and A06 moving off the end position), and relations/successors (A06's only observed successor is now A02, and A01, A03 and A04 invariably precede A02). The all-or-nothing participation change with empirical strength near 0.995 is not the kind of difference sampling fluctuation between two 200-case windows produces. The main limitation is that the evidence cannot distinguish a genuinely new activity from one that already existed but was not executed in the earlier window (0 of 200 cases); it also shows only that A02 now closes every case, not what makes it mandatory [OCC001, POS001, POS005, DIR005, REL003, REL006].

Other differences: small routing shifts not part of this hypothesis — from A03, the share continuing to A06 fell from about 41 to 32 in 100 while shares to A05 and A04 rose (about 37 → 41 and 22 → 27 in 100); from A04, the share going to A06 rose from about 11 to 16 in 100; A05's participation rose slightly from about 50 to 53 in 100 cases; A05's immediate self-repeats became less frequent (lag-1 share about 34% → 21%) and A03–A04 became more often directly consecutive (86% → 95% at distance 1). These are small shifts, some based on fewer than 60 traces, so sampling differences between the windows remain a plausible explanation for them [DIR002, DIR003, OCC002, LAG011, LAG005].
